original_question: Which closed simply-connected 4-manifolds admit a 5-colored graph Γ in G_s^(4) and a cyclic permutation ε of the color set such that g_{ε0,ε2,ε4} = 1 and g_{ε1,ε3,ε4} = 1 and the associated T(Γ, ε) is a gem-induced trisection, so that the trisection genus equals the second Betti number β2(M)? More generally, can one characterize topologically the 4-manifolds that admit gems satisfying the hypotheses used in Proposition 26, or at least identify broad classes of manifolds that do so?
target_in_paper: The draft is aiming at the concluding open problem motivated by Proposition 26 of the paper’s gem/trisection discussion: namely, to topologically characterize the 4-manifolds that admit weak semi-simple crystallizations (or equivalent gem data) giving rise to gem-induced trisections of minimal possible genus; in the closed simply-connected case, this is the problem of characterizing those PL 4-manifolds for which Proposition 26 forces g_GT(M)=g_T(M)=β₂(M).
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the main geometric setting (closed simply-connected 4-manifolds), the relevant combinatorial objects (5-colored graphs/gems, cyclic permutations of colors, residue counts g_{i,j,k}), the need that T(Γ,ε) be a gem-induced trisection, and the intended consequence that the trisection genus equals β₂(M). It also correctly recognizes that Proposition 26 is the nearby result driving the question.
missing_details: The paper works in the PL category; the manifold should be described as a closed simply-connected PL 4-manifold, not just a topological 4-manifold.

The relevant hypothesis is not just two isolated equalities such as g_{ε0,ε2,ε4}=1 and g_{ε1,ε3,ε4}=1; the paper’s actual organizing notion is that of a weak semi-simple crystallization with respect to a cyclic permutation ε.

In the closed simply-connected case, weak semi-simplicity means the full family of residue equalities g_{ε_i,ε_{i+2},ε_{i+4}}=1 for all i mod 5, not merely the two color-4 triples written in the draft.
The proposition is formulated for crystallizations/gems in the paper’s precise sense; the draft should state whether Γ is arbitrary in G_s^(4) or a crystallization of M.
The notation g_{i,j,k} should be defined stand-alone as the number of {i,j,k}-colored residues of Γ.

It is not automatic that T(Γ,ε) is a gem-induced trisection from the residue equalities alone; the handlebody condition on H_{12} (or an equivalent combinatorial criterion from the paper) must still be imposed.

If the question is meant to match the paper’s broader nearby discussion, it should ask for a topological characterization of manifolds admitting weak semi-simple crystallizations giving rise to gem-induced trisections, not for an arbitrary characterization of manifolds with genus equal to β₂(M).

The draft omits the paper’s more general compact-with-boundary context, where the same weak semi-simple framework yields a more general formula for g_GT(M); if one wants only the closed simply-connected case, that restriction should be stated explicitly.
To connect to ordinary trisection genus g_T(M), one must use the paper’s fact that gem-induced trisections are actual trisections only in the closed orientable case.
refined_question: Give a topological characterization of the compact PL 4-manifolds M with empty or connected boundary that admit a weak semi-simple crystallization Γ with respect to some cyclic permutation ε of Δ_4 and such that T(Γ,ε) is a gem-induced trisection. In particular, which closed simply-connected PL 4-manifolds admit such a Γ and ε (equivalently, in this closed simply-connected case, a crystallization with g_{ε_i,ε_{i+2},ε_{i+4}}=1 for every i mod 5), so that Proposition 26 applies and yields g_GT(M)=g_T(M)=β₂(M)?
justification: The draft is not really asking to classify manifolds from two ad hoc residue equalities; it is trying to capture the paper’s open-ended classification problem that arises after the weak semi-simple/Proposition 26 mechanism is explained. The paper’s nearby context first emphasizes that gem-induced trisections directly give genuine trisections only for a restricted class of closed orientable 4-manifolds, and then highlights broad families for which trisections from colored triangulations are genus-minimizing. The earlier paper summarized by the survey identifies weak semi-simple crystallizations as the exact graph-theoretic hypothesis under which the relevant gem-induced trisection has minimal central-surface genus, and in the closed simply-connected case this collapses to the statement g_GT(M)=g_T(M)=β₂(M). So the sharp stand-alone research question is to characterize topologically the manifolds admitting weak semi-simple crystallizations that actually give gem-induced trisections, with the closed simply-connected case singled out as the β₂(M)-equality case.
